inputs_used: head/tail + key-cardinality/target scan of data/train.csv, data/test.csv, data/sample_submission.csv
forbidden_inputs_avoided: no training or model fitting was performed at this stage
task_family: time-series forecast (daily balanced panel regression; 75 country x store x product series)

data_shape.panel_completeness: complete and balanced: 75 x 1826 = 136950 train rows, 75 x 365 = 27375 test rows; zero nulls

product: Using LLMs to Improve Your Coding
Using LLMs to Train More LLMs
Using LLMs to Win Friends and Influence People
Using LLMs to Win More Kaggle Competitions

data_shape.key_overlap: identical country/store/product level sets in train and test — no unseen categories

target.name: num_sold
target.note: strictly positive integer counts; SMAPE's zero singularity is not triggered by the target itself

data_shape.id: monotone integer, disjoint: train 0..136949, test 136950..164324; encodes (date, country, store, product) ordering

test_window.evidence: test dates span 2022-01-01..2022-12-31, strictly after train 2017-01-01..2021-12-31 with zero date overlap; id ranges disjoint and contiguous after train; every (country, store, product) series present in test also appears in train, so the split is a pure forward time cut, not a group holdout

split_policy.scheme: time-based expanding-window CV on whole years: fold k trains on years < y_k and validates on year y_k (2019, 2020, 2021); final refit on 2017-2021 to predict 2022
split_policy.forbidden: shuffled KFold and any row-level random split — the 75 parallel series make same-day information leak across rows; measured ~4.5x optimism on this exact competition (4.56 shuffled vs 20.41 time-split SMAPE, TASK-TS-FUTURE)
extra_cautions: GroupKFold on series id is also wrong: test holds the SAME series, only later in time — the generalization axis is time, not group

all CV folds lie inside the training range and therefore cannot score the extrapolation advantage that ratio_target exists for; read fold scores as a lower bound on that operator's value (open caveat in injection_operators.md)
2020 carries a COVID-shaped regime break; report per-year fold scores, never only the mean
any lag/rolling feature must be computed within-series and shifted so no value at/after a fold's start leaks backward
blend weights must be fit on the same forward folds, else they inherit the same optimism as the base models

metric.name: SMAPE
traps: asymmetric: under-prediction is penalized harder than over-prediction of equal absolute size, so the SMAPE-optimal point forecast sits below the conditional mean and plain L2 on the raw target is misaligned
scale-free / relative: a low-volume series row weighs as much as a high-volume one, so an RMSE-driven model over-serves the large series; per-series normalization matters
target min is 2, so the zero singularity does not bite, but predictions must still be clamped to a positive floor
L1 on log(num_sold) is a tractable surrogate for the relative-error geometry
integer target: rounding may help or hurt — decide on CV, and compute rounding/clamping inside the metric function so every fold and every blend candidate is scored on the post-processed vector

external_data.rules_status: permitted — config.yaml special_rules.external_data_allowed: true, verified 2026-07-29 against official rules 7.C (publicly available at no cost)
external_data.reasoning: The country dimension carries level information no in-file covariate explains: five economically very different countries share identical store/product/date structure, so cross-country differences in num_sold act as a country-level multiplier. Per-country share of yearly total is near-constant (std across 2017-2021: Spain 0.0055, Canada 0.0088, Japan 0.0129, Estonia 0.0135, Argentina 0.0159), the signature of a proportional level covariate. The test year 2022 lies entirely outside the training range, so the level must be supplied by a covariate rather than learned as a feature.

candidates.source: World Bank Open Data — GDP per capita, constant prices (NY.GDP.PCAP.KD) or PPP-constant
candidates.leakage_rule: only values dated <= the prediction year; lag=0 (same-year allowed, historical-solution convention). 2022 may be unpublished at snapshot time — carry_forward the last available year and log the snapshot date
candidates.note: constant-price/PPP mandatory: current-USD moved Japan -14.5% vs Argentina +30.0% for 2021->2022 (14.6 pp spread) versus 3.0 pp for the constant series; a nominal covariate would inject FX and inflation into the prediction

candidates.leakage_rule: deterministic future — no leakage; safe to generate for 2022

candidates.note: region/hemisphere grouping so seasonal harmonics can flip sign for Argentina (southern) against the four northern countries

external_data.whitelist_check: all candidates come from the External-data whitelist in knowledge/task_priors.md. Considered and rejected: Exchange rates (ECB SDMX) — no currency column and a constant-price GDP series deliberately excludes FX. OWID COVID — see not_recorded, it can only be a train-side diagnostic here.
external_data.in_data_fallback_if_blocked: the country multiplier is estimable from official data alone: per-country share of daily total is near-constant across years and can serve as a learned ratio, which the GDP join is a smooth, extrapolable proxy for

injection_ideas.rationale: test window is a strictly future year; a shuffled split measured 4.56 vs 20.41 SMAPE on this competition (~4.5x optimism). The split decision is binding on the evaluator, which must fail loudly if it cannot honor it. Three expanding whole-year folds validate 2019, 2020, 2021.

The 2022 test year lies outside the training range and the country level is what differs across series, so the extrapolation argument says the covariate must carry the level. RACE THIS AGAINST THE join_feature ARM: measured on the real private leaderboard at matched single configuration this form scored 52.073 against join_feature's 48.497, so the argument is sound and the measurement disagrees with it. CV ranks this form first (7.793 vs 9.379) and is wrong; a held-out-year protocol also ranks it first and is also wrong.

The second required arm for the same judgment. A GBDT cannot extrapolate a feature past its training range, which predicts this form should fail on a future test year -- and on both competitions measured so far it won anyway (s3e19 private 48.497 vs 52.073; tps-sep-2022 23.390 vs 24.091, both paired-test significant). Emitted because no local signal we have tested can choose between the forms.

Pairs with ratio_target: the covariate carries the cross-sectional level, this term carries the year drift common to all 75 series, which is otherwise inextrapolable past 2021. Ablating the equivalent year_c term on tpsjan22 cost 4.83 -> 6.02 on the 2017 fold.

Daily retail-like panel keyed by country x store x product — the calendar trigger. Holidays are a deterministic future so 2022 flags are generable without leakage; the per_name + displacement-window form is the stronger one (tpsjan22 pooled flag -> per-name window, 5.46 -> 4.19) and captures year-end/new-year displacement, which matters because the test year starts on 2022-01-01.

Static, in-training-range covariate, so the join_feature form is correct here (no extrapolation involved). Argentina is southern-hemisphere and the other four northern, so a shared seasonal harmonic must be allowed to flip sign rather than be averaged across countries.

2020 is a COVID-shaped regime the official files cannot describe and the 2022 test year does not share; down-weight rather than delete, and flag so the model can separate the regime from the trend. On sep-2022 the same remedy for a broken year was only partial (11.807 -> 11.515), so the weight must be tuned on CV, not assumed.

SMAPE is MAE-family and the target is a strictly positive integer, so rounding and a positive floor belong inside the metric function where every CV fold and blend candidate sees them; global_scale absorbs the level offset SMAPE's asymmetry rewards (the optimal point forecast sits below the conditional mean).

task_prior_match_notes.TASK-TS-FUTURE: date column present, test year 2022 strictly after train 2017-2021 — mandatory time split plus the level-covariate-carries-the-level rule
task_prior_match_notes.TASK-TS-CALENDAR: daily series keyed by country x store x product — exact trigger; calendar + holiday joins indicated
task_prior_match_notes.TASK-MAE-METRIC: SMAPE is an MAE-family relative metric — L1 objective and postprocessing-inside-the-metric apply
task_prior_match_notes.TASK-CAT-ONLY: partial: every non-date feature is categorical but all are low-cardinality (5/3/5), so native-categorical GBDT handling is a baseline, not 'the whole game'; no operator in the vocabulary expresses it (see not_recorded)
task_prior_match_notes.TASK-BLEND-DECOR: forward-looking, applies once a member pool exists; no operator expresses it (see not_recorded)

eda_must_verify: confirm the forward time split and that no (country, store, product) series is truncated or padded

run the proportionality diagnostic per year on total(group)/gdp_pc_const before ratio_target fires — the prior says 0.006-0.017 (proportional), but the operator is conditional and the check is the gate
run covariate_volatility_check on the chosen GDP indicator (flag if cross-country moves exceed 8 pp) to confirm the constant-price series was fetched, not the current-price one
quantify the 2020 regime break per country: magnitude, duration, and whether 2021 returned to the 2017-2019 trend (decides the sample_weight value, or whether 2021 also needs one)
test whether per-country / per-store / per-product shares of the daily total are constant over time (validates both the multiplicative structure and the GDP-proxy hypothesis)
check day-of-week and day-of-year seasonality per country, specifically whether Argentina's seasonal phase is inverted
run the controlled split experiment (shuffled KFold vs forward time split) on one baseline and record both numbers to confirm the ~4.5x optimism prior on this data
confirm the World Bank snapshot's last covered year for each of the five countries so carry_forward's extent for 2022 is logged, not implicit
